# Constant-resistance Joule heating

One theory unit: electrical dissipation follows `P = I^2 R` under steady
current and constant, nonnegative resistance. The model uses standard ISQ
current, resistance and power quantities. Its view requires current and
resistance inputs and exports dissipated power.

Temperature dependence, transient storage and spatial distributions are outside
the model. The relation is authored in SysML and checked by the pinned Pilot.
Static composition does not solve the equation or establish physical evidence.
Winding-loss and resistor-heater examples reuse exactly this release.
